'''Ultra Mobile''' is an American mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) that provides prepaid wireless service on the T-Mobile network. The company is known for plans that include international calling. It is owned by T-Mobile US, which acquired its parent company, Ka'ena Corporation, in 2024.<ref>{{cite news | title=T-Mobile acquired Ultra Mobile. |url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20230314006075/en/T- Mobile-to-Acquire-and-Turbocharge-Mint-Mobile-and-Ultra-Mobile- Brands-Will-Continue-Delivering-Value-on-the-Un-carriers-5G- Network | work=[[Businesswire]] |date=March 15, 2023| url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==History==
Ultra Mobile was co-founded by CEO David Glickman, who had previously founded [[TelePacific Communications]], Justice Technology, and Primo Connect.<ref name=how/>

By 2016, Ultra Mobile products were available in over 25,000 retail stores in the US, including [[Target Corporation|Target]] and [[7-Eleven]].<ref name=how>{{cite news| title=The Phone Companies People Actually Love |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-02-04/the-phone-companies-people-actually-love | work=[[Bloomberg Businessweek]] | last=Kharif| first=Olga |date=February 4, 2016| url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Blakely| first1=Lindsay| title=How This Entrepreneur Started America's Fastest-Growing Company (Twice) |url=https://www.inc.com/magazine/201509/lindsay-blakely/2015-inc5000-a-telco-giant-killer-stalks-another-target.html | work=[[Inc. Magazine|Inc.]] |date=September 2015}}</ref>

In January 2016, the company acquired rights from [[Univision Communications]] to manage the Univision Mobile brand, another T-Mobile [[mobile virtual network operator]] which specializes in US SIM-based international calling plans for calls to Latin American countries.<ref>{{cite news|title=Univision y T-Mobile ponen fin a su alianza para Univision Mobile |url=https://www.cnet.com/es/noticias/univision-mobile-alianza-ultra-mobile-2016/ |last=Martínez |first=Laura  | work=[[CNET]] |date=January 29, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release| url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/univision-mobile-powered-by-ultra-mobile-to-offer-customers-unlimited-domestic-and-international-talk--text-300212410.html   |title=Univision Mobile, Powered by Ultra Mobile, to Offer Customers Unlimited Domestic and International Talk and Text | publisher=[[PR Newswire]] |date=January 29, 2016}}</ref>  In May 2017, Ultra Mobile announced that it was closing down the Univision Mobile brand and that it would automatically transfer all Univision Mobile subscribers to Ultra Mobile.<ref>{{Cite news| url=https://bestmvno.com/ultra-mobile/ultra-mobile-introduces-flex-plans-shuts-univision-mobile/ |title=Ultra Mobile Introduces Flex Plans, Shuts Down Univision Mobile |work=BestMVNO |date=2017-05-18}}</ref>

In August 2016, Ultra Mobile launched [[Mint Mobile]], formerly Mint SIM, an online-only MVNO specializing in prepaid mobile plans on the T-Mobile cellular network, which provides discounted pricing based on monthly, quarterly, or yearly terms paid in advance.<ref>{{cite news |title=Get three months of Mint SIM cell service for $35 |url=https://www.cnet.com/news/get-3-months-of-mint-sim-cell-service-for-35/  |last=Broida |first=Rick | work=[[CNET]] |date=November 16, 2016}}</ref>

In 2017, the company had approximately 150 employees in the US, Europe, and Asia, and had focused on hiring [[millennials]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ultra Mobile CEO David Glickman finds his calling | url=https://www.latimes.com/business/la-fi-himi-glickman-20170205-story.html| last1=White| first1=Ronald D. | work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=February 5, 2017 | url-access=limited}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=How I managed millennials to $100 million in sales | url=https://www.cnbc.com/2015/03/26/how-to-build-a-100-million-business-in-two-years.html | last1=Glickman | first1=David | work=[[CNBC]] | date=March 26, 2015}}</ref>

In November 2019, the [[corporate spin-off]] of [[Mint Mobile]] from Ultra Mobile was completed<ref name=accolades>{{Cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/news/story/2021-10-21/employee-centric-mint-mobile-in-costa-mesa-given-accolades-for-workplace-culture | title=Employee-centric Mint Mobile in Costa Mesa given accolades for workplace culture | first=SUSAN | last=HOFFMAN | work=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=October 21, 2021 | url-access=limited}}</ref> and [[Ryan Reynolds]] acquired a 20%-25% ownership stake in Mint Mobile.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/ryan-reynolds-now-owns-mint-mobile/ | title=Ryan Reynolds now owns Mint Mobile | first=Oscar | last=Gonzalez | work=[[CNET]] | date=November 25, 2019}}</ref> Reynolds and founder Glickman both served on the [[board of directors]] for [[The Michael J. Fox Foundation]] and Glickman was impressed with how Reynolds handled marketing for ''[[Deadpool (film)|Deadpool]]''.<ref name=glickman>{{Cite web | url=https://www.pressreader.com/usa/inc-usa/20210901/283957475584629 | title=David Glickman | work=[[Inc. (magazine)|Inc.]] | via=[[PressReader]] | date=September 1, 2021}}</ref>

In March 2023, [[T-Mobile US]] agreed to acquire [[Mint Mobile]] and Ultra Mobile for up to $1.35 billion.<ref>{{Cite press release | 
url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20230314006075/en/T-Mobile-to-Acquire-and-Turbocharge-Mint-Mobile-and-Ultra-Mobile-Brands-Will-Continue-Delivering-Value-on-the-Un-carrier%E2%80%99s-5G-Network | title=T-Mobile to Acquire and Turbocharge Mint Mobile and Ultra Mobile, Brands Will Continue Delivering Value on the Un-carrier's 5G Network | publisher=[[Business Wire]] | date=March 15, 2023}}</ref> On May 1, 2024, the announcement was published that the planned acquisition was completed as per the agreement.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.t-mobile.com/news/business/t-mobile-closes-acquisition-mint-and-ultra-mobile|title=Mint and Ultra: Welcome to the T‑Mobile Family!|work=T-Mobile|access-date=2025-10-24|language=en}}</ref>

In July 2025, Ultra Mobile changed its logo from a SIM-card design to a globe design as part of a brand refresh.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2025 |title=Ultra Mobile Doubles Down on Value and Savings |url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250630983714/en/Ultra-Mobile-Doubles-Down-on-Value-and-Savings-More-Data.-More-Perks.-2012-Prices. |website=[[Businesswire]]}}</ref>

In May 2026, Ultra Mobile introduced international roaming passes for short-term travel, covering data, calls and texts outside the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 20, 2026 |title=Ultra Mobile Makes International Travel Easier |url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/ultra-mobile-makes-international-travel-easier-with-new-5-roaming-passes |website=[[pcmag]]}}</ref>

== Products and Services ==
Ultra Mobile sells prepaid plans that run on the T-Mobile 5G network. Plans are available in 1, 3, 6 and 12-month terms, with longer terms priced lower per month. All plans include international calling and texting to 90 countries.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 20, 2026 |title=Ultra Mobile Makes International Travel Easier |url=https://www.cnet.com/deals/take-50-ultra-mobiles-8gb-plan-and-pay-just-9-per-month/ |website=[[pcmag]]}}</ref>

In 2026, BestPhonePlans named Ultra Mobile its Top Pick for International Calling.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026 |title=Best Phone Plans |url=https://www.bestphoneplans.net/plans/ultra-mobile-unlimited |website=[[BestPhonePlans]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 18, 2025 |title=Take 50% Off Ultra Mobile’s 8GB Plan |url=https://www.cnet.com/deals/take-50-ultra-mobiles-8gb-plan-and-pay-just-9-per-month/ |website=[[CNET]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026 |title=How Ultra Mobile Works |url=https://www.ultramobile.com/how-it-works/ |website=[[Ultra Mobile]]}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2015, Ultra Mobile was ranked number 1 in [[Inc. (magazine)|Inc.]] magazine's list of the 5,000 fastest growing private companies in the United States, with a year-over-year growth rate of 100,849% and revenues of [[US$]]118 million in 2014, up from less than a million in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Ultra Mobile Tops Inc. 5000 |url=https://www.ocbj.com/news/2015/aug/13/ultra-mobile-tops-inc-5000/ | work=Orange County Business Journal| date=August 13, 2015}}</ref>

WhistleOut rated Ultra Mobile 3.0 to 3.5 out of 5 stars in 2023, and 4.0 to 4.5 overall in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 1, 2024 |title=The Best 4 Ultra Mobile Plans |url=https://www.whistleout.com/CellPhones/Guides/best-ultra-mobile-plans |website=[[whistleOut]]}}</ref>
